headline: A record July import heat dome is feeding a proof, cost and input-friction queue.
dek: The visible weather is import front-loading. The operating weather is the queue behind it: booking decisions, forced-labor proof, freight and diesel repricing, and strategic-input approvals.

zones.name: Covered U.S. ports
zones.operator_meaning: NRF/Hackett expects 2.47M TEU in July, above the May 2022 record, before August-November turn negative YoY.
zones.watch: Reported July TEU by port and origin; whether China-origin strength persists.

zones.name: June import anchor
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters/Descartes reported 2,400,627 TEU in June, +8.2% YoY, with China-origin volume +27.4% to 814,474 TEU.
zones.watch: Order quality and inventory-to-sales data that separate demand from timing.

zones.name: Forced-labor proof clock
zones.operator_meaning: USTR posted July 7-9 Section 301 forced-labor hearing transcripts, turning policy monitoring into SKU-level proof work.
zones.watch: Transcript categories, product examples, final action timing and exemption arguments.

zones.name: Freight and diesel costs
zones.operator_meaning: Drewry's 9 July WCI headline rose 2% to $4,639 per 40ft; Reuters reported U.S. ULSD futures +11% and inventories down to 97.8M barrels.
zones.watch: Clean WCI lane table, diesel futures, gasoil premiums and surcharge treatment.

zones.name: Manufacturing and services inputs
zones.operator_meaning: ISM June Manufacturing and Services stayed expansionary with high Prices and slower Supplier Deliveries; data-center commodities remain short.
zones.watch: July ISM prices, supplier deliveries, imports, backlog and shortage lists.

zones.name: Field to fork
zones.operator_meaning: FAO's headline food index slipped slightly while vegetable oils and meat rose; food exposure needs category, fuel and cold-chain review.
zones.watch: Vegetable oils, meat, weather-linked inputs, diesel and refrigeration capacity.

reference_cards.label: NRF/Hackett July forecast
reference_cards.note: Above May 2022 covered-port monthly record; later forecast air pocket.

reference_cards.label: Drewry WCI
reference_cards.note: 9 July headline, +2%; lane table requires re-check.

reference_cards.label: Diesel station
reference_cards.note: Reuters reported U.S. ULSD futures at $154/bbl and inventories at 97.8M barrels.

reference_cards.label: ISM Manufacturing / Services
reference_cards.note: Expansion with sticky prices and slower deliveries.

reference_cards.label: USTR proof clock
reference_cards.note: Day 1-3 forced-labor Section 301 hearing transcripts posted.

operator_translation: Do not read July volume as one signal. Split it into booking, proof, cost and strategic-input lanes; assign owners before early receipts, proof gaps and repricing pressure land in the same meeting.
operator_watchlist: Reported July TEU by port and origin.
USTR transcript categories and final action timing.
Drewry WCI lane re-check plus diesel inventory updates.
ISM July prices, supplier deliveries, imports and backlog.
FAO category movements for vegetable oils, meat and weather-linked inputs.

newsletter_insert.title: Supply Chain Weather
newsletter_insert.headline: A record July import heat dome is feeding a proof-and-booking queue.
newsletter_insert.body: The weather map is not one blended risk score. Covered-port forecasts, reported June TEU, USTR transcripts, Drewry WCI, diesel, ISM and FAO are separate stations this week. Together they show a decision queue: what to book, what to prove, what to reprice and what to protect.
newsletter_insert.operator_translation: Before approving the next pull-forward move, put exposed product families on a four-lane board: booking, proof, cost and strategic inputs. Name the owner and approval gate for each lane.
